extracted.intended_audience: MathOverflow users deciding whether to apply the 'soft-question' tag (askers and taggers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for when to use the 'soft-question' tag on MathOverflow: which kinds of questions belong under this tag and which do not, plus where to redirect other question types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: research or job-related questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions that are about research in mathematics, or about the job of a research mathematician, without being mathematical problems or statements in the strictest sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this tag for questions concerning research in mathematics or the professional aspects of being a research mathematician, where the question is not itself a formal mathematical problem or statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not for easy or supposedly easy mathematical questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use this tag for easy or supposedly easy mathematical questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a question is an ordinary elementary problem (even if allegedly 'soft' because informal), it should not be tagged 'soft-question' on MathOverflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redirect more elementary mathematics to Math.StackExchange
rubrics_metrics.description: More elementary questions in mathematics are better asked on https://math.stackexchange.com/
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the question is elementary in scope or level, the author should post it on Math.StackExchange rather than MathOverflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redirect teaching questions to Mathematics Educators
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about teaching mathematics are welcome on https://matheducators.stackexchange.com/.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the primary focus of the question is pedagogy or teaching practice, it belongs on the Mathematics Educators site rather than under MathOverflow's 'soft-question' tag.
